proximity.reference_search_domain: Selected inclusive cuboid only; outside reference signal is not searched.
proximity.definition: Directed nearest occupied voxel-centre Euclidean distances using Z/Y/X sampling. The fraction is P(distance <= threshold | source foreground voxel), with equal voxel weighting. It is not a molecule-to-molecule distance, intensity fraction, binding probability or significance test. Direction reversal changes the denominator. Registration, label offsets and optical resolution remain acquisition limitations.

cases.answer: No, swapping the foreground labels will not result in the same fraction because proximity is a directed measure [interpretation]. The denominator is controlled by the source foreground voxels in the direction of the calculation [interpretation]. For example, the marker-to-reference fraction uses the source marker's foreground voxels as the denominator, while the reference-to-marker fraction uses the reference signal's foreground voxels [interpretation]. Proximity is a directed, equally voxel-weighted fraction rather than an intensity-weighted measure [interpretation]. Hypothesis: To determine the effect of swapping, you would need to re-run the analysis with the reversed direction to see how the denominator changes based on the voxel counts of the new source channel.

cases.answer: A nearest distance of zero does not establish molecular contact or zero separation [interpretation]. It indicates that the voxel centers of the two foreground objects are coincident in the selected cuboid [interpretation]. Neither finding overcomes the optical resolution limits of the microscope, as voxel-center coordinates are limited by the sampling and resolution of the acquisition [interpretation]. Proximity measurements use separate Z/Y/X sampling for calibrated voxel-center distances [interpretation]. These sampling differences mean that a distance of zero in one dimension does not imply the same physical proximity in another [interpretation].
